text: Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us and welcome to Coca-Cola Company's
third quarter 2026 earnings results conference call.
After today's prepared remarks, we will host a question and answer session.
If you would like to ask a question, please press star one to raise your hand.
To withdraw your question, press star one again.
I will now hand the conference over to Todd Beiger,
Vice President and Head of Investor Relations. Mr. Beiger, please go ahead.
Good morning and thank you for joining us. I'm here with Henrique Braun, our Chief Executive
Officer, and John Murphy, our President and Chief Financial Officer. We've posted
schedules under financial information in the investor section of our company website.
These reconcile certain non-GAAP financial measures that may be referred to this morning
to results as reported under generally accepted accounting principles.
You can also find schedules in the same section of our website to provide
analysis of our gross and operating margins. This call may contain forward-looking statements,
including statements concerning long-term earnings objectives, which should be considered in
conjunction with cautionary statements contained in our earnings release and the company's
periodic SEC reports. Following prepared remarks, we will take your questions.
Please limit yourself to one question. Re-enter the queue to ask follow-ups.
Now, I will turn the call over to Henrique.
Henrique Braun, Chief Executive Officer, Co-Occola System
Thanks Todd, and good morning everyone. Our third quarter results reinforce the continued
strength of the Co-Cola system. We are acting with speed and discipline, enabling us to
deliver strong results in an uneven environment. I want to start by thanking all our associates
and bottling partners around the world. Every day, they serve customers, support communities,
and bring our brands to life. This year has required resilience, agility, and strong
execution, and our people have continued to rise to the occasion. Their efforts
reinforce my confidence in our updated 2026 guidance and in the long-term opportunities
ahead. This morning, I will provide an update on the global landscape and review
our third quarter business performance. Then, I will discuss how our system is delivering
at scale and adapting locally to create durable growth. John will close with our
financial results for the quarter, full year 2026 guidance, and some early considerations
for 2027. First, the global operating environment continues to evolve.
Geopolitical disruptions affect several parts of the world,
cost pressures have accelerated, and all of this has an impact on many consumers.
Yet, our confidence in the long-term opportunity remains unchanged.
We have a strong portfolio of $32 billion brands and unmatched system reach with our
botling partners. These advantages matter, but so does what we do with them.
For several years, we have been strengthening capabilities around consumer recruitment,
digital, revenue growth management, and system execution. By staying close to consumers and
remaining constructively discontented, we continue to adapt in a dynamic environment.
We are increasingly seeing that work reflected in our performance, including this quarter.
Volume grew 5% and organic revenue grew 7%. Stepping back, our longer-term performance
reflects a more balanced contribution to top-line growth. We expanded margins while
continuing to invest in our business. We delivered double-digit comparable earnings
per share growth and gained value share. Beyond the headline numbers, I'm encouraged by how we
are growing. Our disciplined investments and digital capabilities are creating momentum across
many of our markets and brands. Yet, we know there is still more work to do.
We continue to sharpen how we turn consumer insights into innovation,
and we are balancing scale and intimacy to drive stronger execution across our system.
Our focus is simple. Keep learning and do a little better every day.
This quarter, I spent much of my time with our people and botling partners in several of our
markets. These experiences always reinforce the importance of understanding local needs
and responding to consumers, a strength of our system across the world.
While every market is different, three themes were consistent. One, affordability is working.
Two, both zero sugar and original taste are recruiting consumers. And three, execution and
local relevance are helping us win. Let me bring each of these to life across our business.
Starting in North America, we grew revenue and gained value share for the quarter. Volume was
even due in part to the timing of the July 4th holiday and temporary challenges in certain
finished goods businesses, but performance improved sequentially each month during the quarter.
Across our total beverage portfolio, we had strong volume growth from many brands, including
trademark Coca-Cola, Fairlife, Powerade, Fresca, and Smartwater. Mr. Pibb continued its success
with another quarter of double digit volume growth. We are applying our learnings from our
strong sports playbook with the next iteration of fan work is thirsty work, which brings
Coca-Cola into football fandom through team packaging, retail activation, and locally relevant fan
experiences. For Halloween, we are pairing Fanta's haunted universe with limited edition
ghost face punch and collectable packaging that brings the experience from screen to shelf.
We're also creating new opportunities across our portfolio. Fairlife expanded its new
nutrition plan offerings with the return of fan favorite vanilla, while Body Armor Fit brings
sports hydration beyond the workout with a sparkly, zero sugar format with caffeine,
electrolytes, and metabolism support. In Latin America, several key markets started the year
facing difficult conditions, but our teams responded with market-based and high-quality
actions that drove meaningful acceleration in the third quarter. We grew volume, delivered
balanced top-line growth, and gained value share with broad-based improvement across the region.
In Mexico, the environment remains challenging, but we are seeing encouraging progress by
combining affordability, strong revenue growth management capabilities, and locally relevant
marketing and discipline execution. In Brazil, momentum remained strong across our total
beverage portfolio. Trademark Coca-Cola delivered another strong quarter, while Sprite and sports
beverages also performed well. We continue to connect our brands with locally relevant
passion points, including the Rock in Rio music festival, the Fanta Festival, and the
While also investing behind growth opportunities across our total beverage portfolio.
In Argentina, the environment remains challenging. We have strong plans in place,
and while there is still more work to do, we are encouraged by progress across the region.
Moving to EMEA and starting with Europe. For the quarter, we grew volume, but we lost
value share in a few key markets in Western Europe, and we are taking actions to improve
performance. Following the FIFA World Cup, we transitioned into soccer activations around
the English Premier League and Bundesliga, while continuing to build everyday consumption
occasions through our MUSE platform. We are complementing these investments in
our MUSE platform. We are complementing these efforts with affordable propositions like our
500ml Supercam, and are continuing to focus on price pack architecture to help us recruit
consumers and drive transactions. In Africa, despite cycling a tough volume comparison,
we gained value share and delivered high single digit volume growth.
We celebrated 75 years of Coca-Cola's system in Nigeria with an end-to-end activation. To meet
evolving consumer needs in South Africa, we adapted an affordable single serve package from
India, giving it a locally relevant name, Moshesha, meaning quick. We also activated our
Springbox rugby team partnership with the Be a Box campaign, a limited edition
collectible player scams. In Eurasia and the Middle East, ongoing geopolitical conflicts
continued to disrupt business in parts of the region. Our system was resilient, delivering
another strong quarter with volume growth and value share gains. From Coke Studio, featuring
Pakistani artists to affordability initiatives, to locally relevant taste innovations like Sprite,
Cool Mint, and Fanta Pomegranate, our teams are adapting to dynamic market conditions.
Finally, in Asia-Pacific, performance varied across our operating units, but we are encouraged
by the progress in many markets. We gained value share and grew volume, revenue and profit,
while price mix remained pressured due to a negative geographic mix and affordability
initiatives. India delivered strong volume growth with each of our top 10 brands growing
double digits. We are expanding our consumer base by scaling both affordability and
premiumization, strengthening execution, and leaning into emerging channels. For example,
we expanded our Sprite and Spicy platform into the QSR channel in India, with meal, combo
activations, social media content, and influencer collaborations, which contributed to Sprite's
volume growth of nearly 20% in the region. In China, the consumer environment remains
subdued, with cautious spending and soft domestic demand. Despite this, we delivered another
strong quarter of volume growth with strength in trademark Coca-Cola and Fanta.
We continue to advance our digital capabilities to create more consumption occasions and
connect with consumers in new ways. These actions are helping us drive immediate consumption
packages and accelerate significant growth across digital commerce and emerging channels.
In Japan, volume declined as consumers remained pressured in a challenging
macroeconomic environment that was heavily impacted by a diverse weather.
For the quarter, we gained share, expanded our consumer base in trademark Coca-Cola,
and accelerated zero-sugar volume growth. We are adapting our offerings and executing to meet
changing needs. In ASEAN and South Pacific, volume growth was broad-based across many key
markets. Affordability, zero-sugar offerings, innovation, and stronger execution are helping
us recruit consumers and create new growth opportunities, including the launch of Coca-Cola
in Thailand. In Vietnam, we are expanding our affordable single-serve package, which is now
available in over 400,000 outlets with high repurchase rates. To sum it all up,
while the global operating environment remains uneven, we are encouraged by the momentum across
our business and believe in our ability to deliver more for more markets and more for more
brands. I'm energized by the progress we're making across the Coca-Cola system.
We are learning as we go, continuing to raise the bar, and finding new ways to create value.
The actions we're taking are helping us deliver today while strengthening our ability to create
value for the long term. With that, I'll turn the call over to John.
Thank you, Enrique, and good morning everyone. Our results once again demonstrate the strength
and adaptability of our business. For the quarter, organic revenue grew 7%. Our unit
cases grew 5%. Our two-year, year-to-date volume growth average of 2% reflects a more
sustained and balanced contribution to top-line revenue growth. Concentrate sales were two
points ahead of unit case volume due to the timing of concentrate shipments. Price mix
grew 1%. This was driven by four points of pricing actions, partially offset by three
points of unfavorable mix, primarily due to geographic mix, timing of investments,
and category mix. Comparable gross margin increased approximately 170 basis points,
and comparable operating margin increased approximately 110 basis points. Both reflect
underlying expansion, currency tailwinds, and a favorable structural impact from last year's
sale of our finished product operations in Nigeria. Importantly, margin expansion
did not come at the expense of investment, and we continue to drive greater productivity
and efficiency across our operations. We are investing behind our brands and executing
revenue growth management strategies that help us better serve consumers across brands,
packages, price points, and occasions. Putting it all together, third quarter comparable earnings
per share of 91 cents reflected an 11% increase, including a two-point benefit from currency tailwinds.
Year-to-date free cash flow was $11.4 billion, an increase versus the prior year.
Our balance sheet remains strong, with our net debt leverage of 1.3 times EBITDA,
which is below our target range of two to two and a half times.
We're continuing to judiciously manage our balance sheet as we await a court decision
related to our ongoing dispute with the IRS. We are confident in our long-term free cash
flow generation and the optionality it gives us as we move through the fourth quarter and
into 2027. Our priorities remain the same. Invest in our business and return capital
to share owners. Now let me turn to guidance for full year 2026.
We now expect organic revenue growth of at least 5%, which includes the impact of slight
de-stocking and six fewer days in the fourth quarter. Our commodity exposure overall remains
manageable. However, we are seeing elevated cost pressures in aggregate driven by increased
logistics and transportation costs. We now expect comparable currency neutral earnings per share
growth, excluding acquisitions and divestitures of at least 9%. Divestitures are now expected
to be an approximate 2% headwind to comparable net revenues and we continue to expect an
approximate 1% headwind to comparable earnings per share. This assumes the pending sale of
Coca-Cola beverages Africa closes during the fourth quarter, subject to regulatory approvals.
Based on current rates and our hedge positions, we continue to expect an approximate one point
currency tailwind to comparable net revenues and continue to expect an approximate three
point currency tailwind to comparable earnings per share for full year 2026.
Our underlying effective tax rate for 2026 is now expected to be 19.7%. This reflects
certain benefits in the current year that we do not expect to repeat going forward.
All in, we now expect comparable earnings per share growth of at least 11% versus $3 in 2025.
Finally, we now expect to generate at least $13 billion of free cash flow in 2026.
There are some considerations to keep in mind for the rest of the year.
As a reminder, the fourth quarter will have six fewer days versus the prior year.
We also now expect slight de-stocking in the fourth quarter. Therefore, we expect concentrate
shipments to slightly trail unit case volume for the full year. For the fourth quarter,
following the anticipated refranchising of CCBA, we expect a four point headwind to comparable
net revenues, a three point headwind to comparable earnings per share and slight margin benefits.
While it is too early to provide specific guidance for 2027,
we do want to share some considerations based on what we know today. Overall,
we expect consumer behaviour to remain largely unchanged, with value being a very important
consideration across all markets and income groups. The investments we've made to date
and the actions we've taken across our business position us to enter 2027 ready to execute.
With respect to commodities, we continue to manage various cost pressures and look for ways
to navigate the environment through productivity initiatives with our cross enterprise
procurement group and using all of our revenue growth management levers.
At the same time, we'll continue to invest behind our brands,
maintain disciplined cost management and focus on expanding margins over time.
With the anticipated refranchising of CCBA, we expect an eight point headwind to comparable
net revenues and a two point headwind to comparable earnings per share, but expect
positive impacts to both our margins and the return profile of our business. Additionally,
as previously announced, we are exploring a potential IPO of our bottling operations in
India and will provide further updates as appropriate. Regarding currency, if we assume
current rates and our hedge positions, there would be a slight headwind to both comparable
net revenues and comparable earnings per share for full year 2027. Many factors could impact
both our currency outlook and broader business outlook between now and when we expect to
provide guidance in February. To summarize, we are pleased with our third quarter performance.
Our proven all weather strategy continues to be our best ally to sustain our momentum
for the rest of the year and into 2027. Across our many markets and operating environments,
our people continue to rise to the occasion and we are grateful for their dedication
every day. With that operator, we are ready to take questions.
Ladies and gentlemen, to ask a question, you'll need to press star one on your
telephone. To withdraw your question, press star one again. In the interest of time,
we ask that you please give yourself to one question. If you have any additional questions,
you may rejoin the queue. Our first question comes from Dara Mosenian from Morgan Stanley.
Please go ahead, your line is open. Hey, good morning. Obviously another very strong unit
case result in Q3 on top of Q2 strength, but the summer results were aided by events such
as the World Cup and favorable weather. So, A, I wanted to touch on those events.
It'd be helpful just what you learn from the summer events with the World Cup and even
America's 250, how you're using technology investments to enable the system to better
activate those events, but also really how you're working to hold on to incremental
customers or greater demand from the existing customers during the events
as you look across your brand portfolio. And then B, just maybe taking it broader,
as you look out to 2027 across the business globally, can you just discuss the challenge
you see from cycling some of these tougher comparisons on the unit case side and how
you think about the system's ability to continue to sustain volume growth going forward? Thanks.
Thank you, Dara. It's great to hear from you. Look, first of all, we're really excited with
the results that we had on Q3 because it shows sustained and steady momentum that we had from
the first half. It was important to continue that through to the Q3, pursuing the numbers
that we're getting more from our markets and more from our categories. And that showed up also
in how we continue to gain value share globally. So, it's 22 consecutive quarters of value share
again. So, we're feeling that we got the right momentum. The strategy is working
in an environment that continues to be very dynamic. To your point about the World Cup,
and specifically here in the U.S., also the 250 campaign, those were great moments for us to
pressure test our end-to-end activation, going from the brand strategy, the innovations that we
brought to life, the revenue growth management and execution coming in a very integrated way.
We showed up really well as a system, not only in North America, but globally. We leveraged that
into Q3 and we're going to continue to leverage this in Q4 and 2027. Parts of the tech, data,
and AI that we used during the World Cup, you're seeing on campaigns like Fanta, Halloween,
that you can see the connected packaging really with great content and going all the way down
to a transaction which brings that ability for us to start pressure test, the opportunities to drive
more engagement all the way to transactions moving forward. So, the plans continue to be
addressed market by market in an environment that continues to be very dynamic.
And we feel good about where we are right now for Q3 and building the plans for 2027 as well.
To the point that you asked as well on what we're going to be bringing in for next year,
I always start with the energy that we see with our botulers, our customers, when
they see our plans here to date and what we are laying up for the rest of the year
next year. Yes, we're cycling year to date, year to date, high volume
year, but we earned that, right, with getting closer to the consumer and building
the flexibility on our plans to develop the right foundations to get where we are.
So, we believe in our momentum, we believe in the plans, a lot still to happen until
we get to next year, but we believe that we have everything that is under our control
to guarantee that we continue to deliver on our long-term algorithm.
Our next question comes from Chris Carey from Wells Fargo Securities. Please go ahead,
your line is open. Hi, good morning everyone. Good morning Chris. A key strategy coming into
the year was to drive more balanced top line across volume and price mix. Certainly,
as noted with Daria's question, you're on track for an exceptional year from a volume
delivery standpoint and you'll have to compare against that going into next year,
as you just noted. But one of the things that I wanted to drill into a bit was
the price mix side, which if it turns out to be about 2% this year, we'll see,
could prove one of the lower price mix years in about a decade.
So, the question is really as you go into 2027, how do you think the price mix strategy
evolves so as to continue to deliver on the commitments that you have around
your top line algorithm? And within that, can you perhaps provide a bit of perspective on
how much control you have over that price mix line? There's clearly a geographic mix,
there's category mix, you have pricing investments this year. And I think underlying
the question is just your ability to have control over the complexion of your top line,
as opposed to there are just these headwinds coming at the price mix line that are perhaps
out of your control as you go into next year. So, I'd love any context on that. Thanks.
Thanks, Chris. A topic close to our hearts here. Let me just take a step back from the
quarter, in fact the last two quarters, and just a reminder that when you think about the
two-year volume keg, it's still around the 2% mark, maybe slightly above that given
the last two quarters. So, we still feel good about the objective to deliver a balanced
revenue algorithm, two to three points volume, two to three points price mix as we move
forward. When you take into account some of the factors that have impacted our price mix
numbers recently, it's worth unpacking a little bit. We mentioned in the script that
we had four points of underlying pricing in the quarter, and that's pretty consistent with
our year-to-date numbers. A little bit of higher inflation from a couple of
markets in the emerging world, but pretty consistent. I think it's the mix piece that
has had a bigger impact on that PMO number, and maybe a little bit of a surprise to some.
Within that, about two-thirds of it relate to actions that either we have taken ourselves
proactively or reflect just some of the inherent mix that has taken place this year,
particularly with the finished goods performance. If you were to factor in the Topo Chico
situation we've had this year, and you factor in the timing of investments,
you take those out. Our price mix for the year is pretty much within the band that we would
look to deliver. Now, as we go into 2027, it's a little early to give specifics on
what we expect for 2027, but just look at the volume keg or the volume momentum that we have
been delivering. We're continuing to look closely across the world at pricing dynamics
going into 2027. Inflation is one factor, but we also take into account a number of other
factors. The state of the consumer market by market, the competitive environment,
customer environment, etc. We provide a little more color in that in Feb, but the mix piece
we'll continue to see some geomix headwinds just given the nature of the overall portfolio
globally with the developing markets will continue, I believe, to outgrow some of
the developed markets volumetrically. Two-thirds of the mix, as I said, this quarter
were due to factors which we think are manageable going into next year.
LORINNE LIEBERMANN Our next question comes from
Lauren Lieberman from Berkley's. Please go ahead. Your line is open.
LORINNE LIEBERMANN Great, thanks. Good morning. I wanted to talk a little bit about
reinvestment. I know the mantra is more with more, and it looks like this quarter,
in terms of the reinvestment that went into SGA, there was a lot of more.
So if you could just talk a bit about how much advertising and marketing was up,
how much of this is sort of a set the stage into 27 because the gross margins,
and also while we're on margins, underlying gross margin, I think, in the slide
was up 70 basis points. So just curious how to think about that. You talked about mix has
actually been a headwind. So is it just the absolute strength of the volume flowing through
that's driving that gross margin strength? So marketing investments, where the SGA dollars
went, and then drivers of the underlying 70 basis points on gross margin. Thanks.
LORINNE LIEBERMANN Yes, Lauren, thank you. Let me start with the gross margin
numbers. As you're well aware, we think of gross margin in three distinctive buckets.
The underlying strength of the business, the structural and currency were benefiting from some
currency headwinds or some currency tailwinds this year. But the underlying numbers just
reflect the quality of top line and the ongoing focus we have on managing our cost base. So
as you think about the underlying going forward, implied in our algorithm is modest expansion,
we believe we have the ability to sustain that as we go forward.
Regarding the marketing investments, yes, we have taken a number of actions in recent months
to set us up for a strong start to 2027. We have double digit growth above the line,
and we have a number of programs that we're working in partnership with our
botters on, as I said, to be ready for a strong start into 2027. I would expect as we go forward
that we will have marketing investments growing more or less in line with
gross margins to get the shape of the P&L where we want it to be, not just for 2027,
but beyond. LORINNE LIEBERMANN Our next question comes from Steve Powers from Deutsche
Bank. Please go ahead. Your line is open. STEVE POWERS Yes, hey, great. Thanks and good morning.
We've spoken about this before, but just the reality is that a lot of the inflationary
pressures facing the system today sit more heavily with your bottling partners than with
the concentrate business itself. And I guess, in that context, as you approach
collective 2027 planning, how would you characterize bottler economics today
and their stance relative to those inflationary pressures, and any impacts that may be having on
considerations around future pricing, investment levels, or just the way that
system economics are shared as you think about the year ahead? Thank you.
LORINNE LIEBERMANN Thank you, Steve. Look, first of all, we always look at that
from a system point of view. Everything starts from how we're going to first grow
our plans aligned with our brand plans per market. And we feel that we have
great plans for 2027, and we are actually anticipating that with investments this year,
as we have done in previous years, to be ahead of the curve, to get the momentum that we have
and the flexibility that we build during the year to continue to invest on those plans.
Regarding costs, which is one input into the plan, the environment remains very fluid.
The commodities have been manageable for us at this time. Looking forward, we are
working with the bottlers right now through all the levers that we have as a system. One
of them is our cross enterprise procurement group that we procure the big commodities that we have
for next year together. And with that, we bring also other levers into the equation,
which is productivity, cost management, and our RGM tools to ensure that we have an
operational environment that can be totally linked with our growth plans for next year.
So more to come as we learn during the next few months, but so far it has been something
that we believe is going to be manageable on the overall scheme of things.
Our next question comes from Filippo Follorini from Citi. Please go ahead, your line is open.
Hi, good morning everyone. I wanted to go back to the North America business.
Enrique, you mentioned that there were a few impacts on the volume being flat on the quarter
time, we go 4th of July and some changes in the finished good business. Can you expand a
little bit more on that? And given we see solid consumption data and track channels,
are you expecting some improvement as we move forward? And then on price mix, I know
you were cycling a difficult comp in Topo Chico and Fairlife. How should we think about that,
particularly that mix component as we look ahead on the price mix in North America?
Thank you. Thank you. So North America, let me step back and talk a little bit about
the quarter and the year so far. We continue to see solid performance
in North America. We grew this quarter, right? Revenue, we gained value share,
we expanded margins. We got pricing in line with inflation that was really important,
but shows that the brands have the equity and the right to take price. And we kept
investing in our brands. The impact that you mentioned on the price mix was definitely
impacted by the cycling of a very strong prior year on some of the premium brands that were
generated through our finished goods, including Topo Chico, one of them that you know,
and Body Armor as well. So with that into the equation, if you take that out,
actually, and you take the impact of the July 4th that fell into the second quarter,
and we mentioned that before, we would see volume grow. So we see the momentum is still there.
Now, in terms of the strength of our strategy and our brand, we also feel confident that we
have pretty good momentum, especially with trademark Coca-Cola that grew again this quarter.
Diet Coke and Coca-Cola Zero, especially Coca-Cola Zero growing double digit again,
and Fair Life continues to do really well. Powerade also grew. And we have other areas
that we have work to do, which is always good for us also to instill here our motto of being
constructive with this content that there are areas for us to work on. And one of them is to do
a better performance on Sprite and Body Armor and our supply chain going into next year.
So all in all, we believe that we have the good momentum as a system and the right plans
to navigate through the rest of the year in 2020-20 south.
Yeah, and I would just add, Filippo, if you're looking at the overall volume number,
the restaurant industry continues to be under pressure. And so when you're looking at the
scanner data, et cetera, I think you're seeing a stronger business at home versus away from
home, largely driven by the consumer pressures that we've talked about in the past. And while
our own business continues to have a lot of momentum across those channels, I think the
underlying pressure across the consumer landscape is there. And I think it will be there for the
rest of the year as we go into 27. Our next question comes from Andrea Tichera
from JP Morgan. Please go ahead. Your line is open. Hi, good morning, everyone. So I have
a question on exploring the theme of affordability. And of course, among all the CPGs,
you have significant brand equity. How should we be thinking about the list pricing
and your bottling partners have historically been able to take pricing in the low single
digits? If we put the geographical mix aside, do you think you still can count on RGM
capabilities and would still allow some selective pricing while protecting the entry
price points? And then a clarification on the fourth quarter. You obviously raised guidance
and you have the six-year selling days. John, you called out also the dis-talking comment,
but you had also had said that in the third quarter. So I was ahead of the third quarter.
So I was hoping to think about how it's a wide range. Of course, minimum five allows you to
have a wide range there. But just thinking how demand and dis-talking and how we should
rethink how many points of headwind that could be. Thank you. Okay, Andrea. So I'll start
with your question, especially on our strategy on the affordability. John can chime in on
the outlook. So look, the affordability, you need to look at this on the full context of
revenue growth management. It's one of the legs of how we get closer to the consumer these
days. The premiumization is equally important. So we always look at both. What we are seeing
across the world, and this is something that especially in my travel the last quarter going
divide and conquering here with John going different parts of the world, we have seen that
value continues to be something that cuts across every market and every consumer that we see all
over the world. And that means different things for the consumer, which then touches into
affordability and premiumization in a way that we capitalize that in our plans. I may
elaborate on that. On the affordability, what we always look at is do we have the right value,
the relevance of that brand, and the worth-choosing option for the consumer to
keep them in the franchise? And if the answer is yes, we continue to push forward and
get more coverage of that packaging format. If not, we adapt our plans and put that in place.
A good example of that is what we did in Africa, piggybacking from what we've learned in India,
where they had one package, which is a single serve PET package with placement technology
that can allow you to go in longer routes and still keep the shelf life high. Now we
imported that into Africa, and that plays on affordability on both of these markets.
And it's going to continue to be very important moving forward because the consumer
loves the brands but needs to be closer to what they can afford. On the premiumization side,
that's equally important on this equation, we play the category mix. There are a few brands
that continue to help us with that. In North America, you've got Core Power,
you've got Smart Water, and you've got in other parts of the world also different packaging sizes
that allows us to play with the convenience. And that value equation for the consumer also
works really well. And in the overall RGM strategy, we end up delivering what we need.
So it goes in tandem, affordability, and premiumization. And that's where you're going
to see not only the rest of the year, but building into 2027. John, if you want to add on that.
Yeah, Andrea, the whole marriage of unit cases with our concentrate shipments this year has
proven to be maybe the more challenging year since I've been around for a few reasons.
You've got the first quarter and the fourth quarter, the plus six, the minus six days.
We have, as we've seen since the start of the year around the world, an external environment
that's quite unpredictable. And I think our system has a tendency to want to get ahead of that.
And so the expectation that we highlighted in guidance reflects the best information
we have at the moment. There's a couple of our segments where we do expect to see
some destocking on the back of what has happened year to date. But we've still got
some distance to go in the year and we're keeping a close eye on this area. And
